questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe no matter how you use it.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of your motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check everything except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your spokes for bending or damage, your tire tread and condition, and all lights. Seat fabric does not need to be checked before every ride.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs tell you the traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: How can you be more easily seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position yourself in your lane to be clearly visible. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move if needed.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle more visible is to:

options.text: Use a large flag attached to your frame.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times and use your turn signals and brake light. Wear bright, reflective clothing to increase visibility.

questions.question: ____ removes alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: Which is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves. Sandals do not provide protection.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift down one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Downshift one gear at a time and ease out the clutch between each shift.

questions.question: What footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laces should be tucked away securely before riding.

questions.question: To get the most helmet protection, choose one that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to stay safe on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Quick moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not use the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but let you move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: Only if you ride for more than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a riding group small is:

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders are always trying to catch up.
It is hard to keep track of everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass safely, stay together better at traffic lights, and don't require slower riders to rush to catch up.

questions.question: When riding on bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge grating may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to avoid the weave is dangerous.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Are stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, impair your riding ability. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows down a motorcycle. Note that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Using signals correctly is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has the same effect as:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle down, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely to protect yourself while riding.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on a motorcycle, you should be ready for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out in front of you. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space to avoid hazards.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will make the driver tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.
